findings.title: Conditional passkey UI is never set up on a normal login page
findings.body: The new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns true only when `user != null` (see the helper at line ~161). On a normal login, where no user is set yet, the call evaluates to false, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped. The passkey conditional UI (the webauth form and autocomplete attributes) is therefore missing from the initial username/password page. The old code filled it when `context.getUser() == null`, so this inverts the condition. The same inversion affects the `challenge(context, error, field)` override at line ~137, which now only fills the passkey form when a user is already set. The new tests that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page (e.g. passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) would fail.

findings.title: Call to zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, but the only overload added in UsernamePasswordForm.java is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. Nothing in this diff declares a no-arg version, so this will not compile unless one exists elsewhere that is not in the change. The intent appears to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: configureTestRealm is called but not defined in the diff
findings.body: `addTestRealms` now calls `configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation)`, but this file does not define it in the diff and no import or visible inheritance source is shown. If it is not defined in AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest, the test class will not compile.

findings.title: Unused NoSuchElementException import left behind
findings.body: After replacing the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` checks with positive assertions, the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is no longer used. Checkstyle or the build's unused-import check may fail on it.

findings.title: Negative webauthn checks use try/catch(Exception) and can pass vacuously
findings.body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the assertion `assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` throws NoSuchElementException when the element is absent, and the `catch (Exception nsee)` swallows it. The check passes whether or not the element exists in the wrong state, except via the unreached fail(). A `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()` check would assert the intended behaviour directly. The same pattern appears at lines ~313-317.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the bug being fixed (passkeys during re-authentication with prompt=login), the behaviour change (username form now shown during re-auth when passkeys are enabled, and the conditional UI setup changes), or the reasoning for the new AuthenticatorUtils helper. Reviewers have no context for these behaviour changes.
